At last I got my composure back, and groaned.
Precious time had been wasted. There was no doubt of it.

I had to move at once.
The sword-armor—that sword-armor was no good.

It was never a thing to be touched.
It would bring calamity. I was certain. I could say it flat out.

...And I was afraid for Hikaru, who had armored herself in a sword-armor like that.
Why had I not stopped her?

The worry did not end there.
How had the fight with the bandits gone? Their numbers were far greater. Even for Hikaru as a warrior, they could not be an easy enemy.

The more I thought, the more the urgency ate at me.
...I had to go into town and see for myself.

Confirming that Hikaru was safe came first.

Nothing could be done about the half-wrecked sanctuary for now.
I would carry my foster mother to a safe place, and then—
